title: Upstream use-after-free and double-free defects in PostgreSQL's memory managers
note: The allocator pin is 17.0; the complete single-user backend port is 17.5. 2026-10-05: a cheribsd-revocation arm was added by this project and run on all 8. The corpus had no plain-purecap arm, only the two PoisonCap ones, and PoisonCap is out of scope for the study these results feed; without it these 8 could not be compared with the other PostgreSQL corpora, which all carry that arm. The build path already existed -- cmake/Replay.cmake builds one hosted executable per case under PG_CORPUS_DIR and says 'plain CheriBSD' when PG_POISONCAP is off -- so nothing in the corpus or the port was changed to produce it. One qualification on reading those 8 silences, because it bites elsewhere: the guest's security.cheri.runtime_revocation_every_free_default is 0, so a revocation sweep runs only once a quarantine threshold is crossed, and a short case that frees a handful of objects may never cross one -- a silence can then mean 'no sweep ran yet' rather than 'the mechanism could not see it'. That confound does NOT apply here, and the reason is worth stating: pfree returns a chunk to its context and never returns the block to malloc, so there is no malloc free for a sweep to act on at any threshold. The silence is a property of the nesting, not of when the quarantine happens to flush. Re-pinned from 17.0 to 17.5 on 2026-10-06, and three cases moved to not-live-at-17-5/ because `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows their upstream fixes are already in REL_17_5: 83ce20d671, 727bc6ac33f6 and 9d5ce4f1a00a. The 17.0 pin was the only one in the PostgreSQL study, and it is what let three already-fixed defects appear in a 17.5 result table. The five that remain all have fixes later than REL_17_5 (2025-05-05): 2025-08-02, 2025-08-30, 2025-10-03, 2025-10-09 and 2026-03-30.
